children: By Rajendra Jadhav and Ashitha Shivaprasad
Gold demand in India picked up modestly this week as a correction in prices drew in buyers ahead of the festive season, while demand across other major Asian hubs remained largely steady.
Indian domestic gold prices (MAUc1) were trading around 150,600 rupees ($1,571.29) per 10 grams on Friday after rising to 164,773 rupees last month, the highest level in nearly six months.
"Sentiment is slowly turning positive as prices come down. Jewellery stores are reporting an improvement in retail demand this week," said an Ahmedabad-based jeweller.
Dealers quoted a discount (XAU-IN-PREM) of up to $43 an ounce over official domestic prices this week, inclusive of 15% import and 3% sales levies, compared to last week’s discount of up to $60.
Discounts were high at the start of the week but narrowed as demand improved and jewellers began making purchases for the festive season, said a Mumbai-based dealer with a private bank.
Indians will celebrate Dussehra festival in October, and Diwali in early November, when buying gold is considered auspicious.
In Singapore (XAU-SG-PREM), gold traded at premiums of $1.70 to $2.50 this week. In Hong Kong (XAU-HK-PREM), premiums ranged from $1.70 to $2.00.
"These tight spreads show a balanced, healthy physical market," said Joshua Rotbart, founder of J. Rotbart & Co.

"High-net-worth clients and family offices are using recent price pullbacks as buying opportunities for physical metals. They aren't trying to trade short-term market noise; they're moving wealth into physical bullion to protect against broader economic uncertainty."
In China, bullion (XAU-CN-PREM) traded at par with global benchmark prices, compared with a premium of $5 an ounce last week.

Jewellery demand has remained weak amid subdued consumer confidence, though investment demand for coins and bars has reportedly held up well in China, said Rhona O'Connell, head of market analysis at StoneX.
In Japan (XAU-TK-PREM), gold traded between a $0.25 discount and a $0.5 premium. Japanese markets were closed until Wednesday due to public holidays.
Dussehra, Diwali festivals due in coming months
